The workers are therefore repeatedly applying small kicks, one-to-three-point hole insertions, soft-max quenches, and the same LP snap-back, which either return to this basin or time out before a genuinely different contact topology is explored; this explains 49 programs producing only an $8.8\times10^{-7}$ tightening. The incumbent is therefore an almost isostatically jammed, rigid vertex: the LP has exhausted linearized slack, small kicks or single-point hole insertions snap back to the same contact graph, and large kicks are rejected by greedy basin-hopping. Repeated record-seeded LP-heavy searches, several of which timed out, are revisiting the same topology rather than exploring new basins. What is missing is a different contact-graph topology containing a collective floppy mode—a subset of under-contacted points and slack pairs, with more balanced load across points—not another microscopic tightening of the current graph.
